sources.title: Artemis II Preliminary Science Report
sources.finding: NASA identifies the episode as a potential sighting by Koch at 23:22:39 UTC through a camera, records the competing mountain and optical-effect interpretations, and concludes that no lofted dust or exospheric glow was definitively detected.

sources.title: Artemis II Preliminary Science Report
sources.finding: NASA maps visible limb features in crew image art002e009280 to the rims of Al-Biruni and Goddard using the NASA/JAXA SLDEM 60 m elevation model. This is a real terrain control for one Earthrise image, not complete event-burst geometry.

sources.title: Artemis II Preliminary Science Report
sources.finding: For art002e009280, NASA obtained a pixel-level terrain match at 23:22:44.5 UTC, 14.2 seconds later than the D5 timestamp 23:22:30.29 UTC. The report treats this as a discrepancy for future analysis, so camera time alone cannot supply exact event geometry.

sources.title: Artemis II Preliminary Science Report
sources.finding: NASA recommends a dedicated low-light camera optimized for limb and horizon observations because it would provide quantifiable measurements of extended faint sources and enable confident detection or non-detection of lofted dust.

sources.title: Artemis II Lunar Science Data User Guide
sources.finding: The D5 viewfinder was used as a magnifying monocle. Window 2 was the preferred 400 mm imaging window, but pre-mission characterization through the complete three-pane stack could not be performed, the panes can distort images, and the D5 cameras were not calibrated to mission-specific science requirements beyond geometric lens distortion.

sources.title: Artemis II Lunar Science Data User Guide
sources.finding: PCD3 recorded Koch and Wiseman during flyby. PCDs and handheld cameras referenced the Orion clock. Transcript UTC was derived from audio metadata after WhisperX alignment and then manually checked; PDS labels carry the audio start time derived from duration and the embedded end time.

sources.title: Artemis II Mission Archives

sources.finding: The 7 October 2026 release includes crew-camera, Orion-camera, and mission-audio data; the SPICE bundle remains marked delayed on the retained 9 October page.
